summary: Transient GPU visibility loss causing stepwise throughput degradation for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC, AtlasDocs (dedicated pool) observed stepwise throughput degradation across their reserved capacity window. The platform reported transient GPU visibility losses on a subset of nodes which triggered autoscaler shrink and forced funneling of traffic to fewer GPUs, increasing p99 latency and reducing sustained throughput.
Impact: Customer-facing inference pipelines experienced 30–40% reduction in tokens/sec for 2 of their primary routes and elevated p99 latency from ~120ms to ~480ms. No user prompts were lost but tail latency caused downstream timeouts in customer orchestration (retry storms).
Timeline highlights:
- 09:12 UTC: first sign of allocation delay spikes (allocation-failures metric up to 1.2%).
- 09:14 UTC: scheduler logged node-agent disconnects; 3 nodes reported GPU visibility loss for 10–25s.
- 09:20 UTC: autoscaler interpreted reduced slot availability and removed 2 warm nodes (shrink), which amplified the throughput impact.
- 09:25–09:50 UTC: intermittent recovery and additional short visibility blips correlated with a background process on some nodes.
Environment: Dedicated cluster reserved for AtlasDocs in us-west-2. Serving runtime: 2026.02.15 build. Node agent: node-agent v1.8.4. Autoscaler: predictive v2.1.
Steps to reproduce (observed on platform):
1) Push a steady 50 RPS of short-stream requests to the tenant's reserved pool.
2) Observe allocation-failures and node-agent disconnects in telemetry.
3) Watch autoscaler decisions (shrink events) following visibility blips.
Observed metrics:
- Allocation failures: baseline 0.3% -> spike 4.5% at peak.
- Throughput (tokens/sec per-tenant): -35% average during incident.
- p99 latency: 120ms -> 480ms.
- Node-side nvidia-smi timeouts correlated with visibility windows.
Logs / pointers:
- Scheduler logs: link to Kibana: /app/kibana/scheduler/logs?range=2026-03-10T09:00:00Z..2026-03-10T10:00:00Z&query=SUP-461223
- Node agent traces: link to tracing: /app/jaeger/traces?service=node-agent&from=2026-03-10T09:12Z&to=2026-03-10T09:30Z
- Autoscaler events: /app/console/autoscale/events?tenant=AtlasDocs&from=2026-03-10
For immediate mitigation:
1) We applied a transient autoscaler override to prevent shrink for the tenant (held desired nodes for 30m) at 09:28 UTC.
2) We quarantined two nodes with repeated GPU visibility blips and rolled traffic to replacements.
3) Requested customer-side config change: increase client-side retry backoff to avoid retry amplification.
Current impact: mitigations restored baseline throughput by 09:40 UTC but residual p99 jitter remains; investigation ongoing.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC - Diego Morales (SRE): We've applied an autoscaler hold for AtlasDocs to prevent further shrink events while we investigate node instability. Quarantined nodes node-uw2-47 and node-uw2-61 for deeper diagnostics.

2026-03-10 09:48 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports that the downstream orchestrator timed out on webhook calls. They increased retry backoff per our suggestion; they want ETA for full resolution.

2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Eng (Liu Chen): Early hypothesis: intermittent PCIe reset or driver watchdog on a subset of Ampere GPUs triggered temporary visibility loss. Need node dmesg and nvidia logs. Asked infra to collect /var/log/messages and /var/log/nvidia-installer.log from quarantined nodes.

2026-03-11 14:20 UTC - Infra (Samir Kapoor): Collected node logs and saw repeated pcie link down/up events on node-uw2-61 around 09:13 UTC. Also observed kernel oops relating to nvlink health probe; possible kernel module regression after 2026-02-20 driver bundle.

2026-03-12 08:10 UTC - Diego Morales: Rolling plan: (1) hold autoscaler for 24h while we schedule kernel/driver rollback on the affected node pool; (2) add additional node-agent health check for GPU visibility and classify short blips under a grace window so autoscaler doesn't immediately shrink. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145

2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - Customer (AtlasDocs - Elena Rojas): Thanks for the quick mitigation. Please advise if you plan to notify us of schedule for longer maintenance; our production window is weekdays 14:00–20:00 UTC.

2026-03-12 15:00 UTC - Aisha Patel: Noted customer maintenance window. Scheduling engineer-led rollback to a previously stable driver for the pool and will send follow-up timeline before change window.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Kernel/driver regression introduced a race that causes ephemeral PCIe/NVLink resets under specific I/O patterns from background sidecars (e.g., checkpoint writers).
Hypothesis B: Node-agent health check had too-tight detection for GPU visibility; short-lived probe failures were considered full GPU loss, leading autoscaler to shrink prematurely.
Telemetry correlation: all visibility blips coincide with elevated host PCIe error counters and a compacted pattern of small-stream IOs on those nodes between 09:10 and 09:25 UTC.

We searched historical incidents and found similar symptoms in INT-98832 (internal platform test reported single-node NVLink read errors on 2026-01-29) but frequency/impact larger here due to production reserved traffic and immediate autoscaler reaction.
Node diag: dmesg shows 'PCIe link down' entries; nvidia-smi showed 'No devices were found' for 8–18s during blips.
action_items: Infra: schedule driver rollback for affected us-west-2 warm pool and run soak tests (owner: Samir Kapoor, ETA: 2026-03-13)
Serving runtime: add small grace window for GPU visibility before autoscaler considers slots lost (owner: Liu Chen, PR drafted)
Support: confirm mitigation timeline with AtlasDocs and provide planned maintenance window that avoids their peak hours (owner: Aisha Patel)
Telemetry: add metric 'gpu-visibility-blip_count' with 1s resolution and alert when >3 blips in 10m for a pool (owner: Diego Morales)
Post-incident: run a focused canary with checkpoint-write heavy workload to reproduce and validate fix (owner: Eng leads, due: 2026-03-16)
Follow-up: determine whether background sidecar IO pattern can be throttled or isolated from GPU-critical paths (owner: Platform PM)
resolution: Mitigations applied (autoscaler hold, quarantined nodes) restored most throughput. Root cause under investigation; top candidate is driver/kernel regression causing intermittent PCIe/NVLink resets that present as GPU visibility loss. Planned rollback and autoscaler grace-window change scheduled. Customer notified and provided temporary guidance to increase retry backoffs. Incident remains open until post-rollback soak and canary validation complete.
final_notes: Avoiding premature autoscaler shrink is highest priority to reduce amplification of transient hardware blips. Will follow up with full timeline and postmortem after fixes are validated.
